correctness.rationale: For 6 vertex, 10 face-center and 15 edge-midpoint icosahedral axes, the addition theorem identifies exact degree-k harmonic evaluation rank with rank of the 31x31 Legendre Gram matrix. Raw coordinate/diagonal congruences put both even and odd degrees in Q(sqrt5). Inspected full standard-library Q(sqrt5) elimination algorithm and its complete stated rank table for k=0..74; rank k=74 is30, k=29 first reaches31. Independent from-scratch C++ modular recurrence and Gaussian elimination evaluated 1700 matrices mod prime10009 under sqrt5=4070: for k0..74 ranks matched the supplied low-degree table, and for k75..1699 ALL 1625 were nonsingular. Nonzero finite-field determinant proves nonzero characteristic-zero determinant because denominators are invertible for recurrence range. For k>=1700, exact separation max cos^2=1/2+sqrt5/6<7/8 yields sinθ>7/20 and Bernstein |P_k|<=sqrt(2/(pi k sinθ)), hence 30 off-diagonal absolute entries have row sum <1. Positive diagonal one gives Gershgorin invertibility. Modular certificate covers finite gap only; analytic bound separately covers infinite k. Independent modular checks support low-degree ranks but the full Q(sqrt5) elimination was inspected, not independently rerun end-to-end.

value.rationale: The union of three natural icosahedral symmetry orbits is a canonical 31-axis configuration. Its exact-degree harmonic interpolation threshold, 1-dimension last defect, and eventual permanent full rank at 75 are a meaningful finite cutoff and complete rank invariant. Parity of antipodal sampling makes 31 the natural full rank.

limitations: Single-degree parity-compatible data on fixed regular icosahedron; not numerical conditioning or arbitrary perturbed axes.
